Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM EDT Sun Sep 20 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Six, located several hundred miles southwest of
the Azores.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Fay (AT1/AL062026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...DEPRESSION STRENGTHENS TO TROPICAL STORM FAY... As of 9:00 AM GMT Sun Sep 20 the center of Fay was located near 33.7, -33.1 with movement NNE at 5 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1004 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 45 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Public Advisory Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM GMT Sun Sep 20 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 200841
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Fay Advisory Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 AM GMT Sun Sep 20 2026
 
...DEPRESSION STRENGTHENS TO TROPICAL STORM FAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM GMT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...33.7N 33.1W
ABOUT 450 MI...730 KM SW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNE OR 20 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM GMT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was
located near latitude 33.7 North, longitude 33.1 West. Fay is moving
toward the north-northeast near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this general 
motion is expected for about another day. A turn to the southwest 
is expected on Monday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 45 mph (75 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Additional strengthening is expected over the 
next day or so.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM GMT Sun Sep 20 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 200842
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 AM GMT Sun Sep 20 2026
 
Deep convection has been increasing near the center of the cyclone
and in curved bands on its north side over the past several hours.
The latest satellite intensity estimates have also increased and
range from 35 to 47 kt. Considering these data and the ASCAT pass
from last night, the initial wind speed is nudged up to 40 kt. This
makes the system Tropical Storm Fay. The storm is quite compact,
with its tropical-storm-force winds estimated to extent only about
40 n mi from the center and the associated convection extends about
100-150 n mi across.
 
The combination of relatively moist air and baroclinic enhancements
from an approaching mid- to upper-level trough should cause Fay to
gain some more strength during the next 12 to 24 hours. However, the
trough is expected to lift out on Monday, and an increase in shear
and intrusions of dry air should end the opportunity for
strengthening and cause weakening by that time. Fay will likely
become a remnant low on Tuesday and dissipate by the end of the week
as it is expected to remain in unfavorable environmental conditions.
The NHC intensity forecast is a little higher than the previous one,
and lies near the high end of the guidance in the short term given
the improvement in the storm's organization and expected baroclinic
support.
 
Fay is drifting to the north-northeast, with the latest initial
motion estimated to be 020/4 kt. This general motion should continue
for about 24 hours. However, a low- to mid-level ridge is
anticipated to build to the north of the storm on Monday, and that
should cause Fay to turn southwestward and gradually accelerate in
that direction during the early and middle portions of the week. The
NHC track forecast is similar to the previous one and near a blend 
of the HCCA, GDMI, and TVCN aids.
